options: New requirements never formally added to the project scope, or added without estimating the impact on the deadline
A change in the data arriving at a machine learning model
The gradual reduction of a project's budget
A datastore that is not accessible
questions.explanation: Scope Creep is those new requirements that are never formally added to the scope, or are added without estimating the impact on time and cost.

questions.stem: In which discipline is Scope Creep a well-known term?
questions.explanation: Scope Creep is a known term in Project Management, but it also impacts data architecture and data modelling.

questions.stem: What does the thumb rule 'TCS' stand for?
questions.explanation: TCS stands for Time, Cost and Scope, the three pillars of project management.

questions.stem: According to the TCS rule, what happens when one of the three pillars is impacted?
options: The remaining two will also be impacted
questions.explanation: Whenever one of Time, Cost or Scope is impacted, the remaining two will also be impacted.

questions.stem: In the example of Scope Creep, what does the Project Manager fail to do when a new requirement is added?
options: Estimate how much more effort is required and whether additional cost is involved
questions.explanation: Scope Creep arises when a requirement is added but the Project Manager does not estimate the extra effort or any additional cost, which may hit the go-live date.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a reason for Scope Creep?
options: Lack of a change management process
questions.explanation: Weak sponsor decisions, missing change management, vague acceptance criteria and bad estimation are all listed causes; cloud resource use is not.

questions.stem: Which reason for Scope Creep concerns things that should have been ruled out early in the project?
options: Non-identification of out-of-scope items earlier in the project lifecycle
Bad management of risks and issues
questions.explanation: Failing to identify what is out of scope early in the project lifecycle is one of the listed reasons for Scope Creep.

questions.stem: What ultimate consequence of Scope Creep does *I Am Datapedia!* say no one wants?
options: An impact on the project go-live date
questions.explanation: At the end of the day Scope Creep may impact the project go-live date, which no one wants.

questions.stem: Why is Scope Creep worth discussing among data professionals?
options: Because it only occurs in data projects
Because it is a type of data validation
Because it can also impact data architecture and data modelling
questions.explanation: Although a project management term, Scope Creep can also impact data architecture and data modelling.

questions.stem: On what does the occurrence of Scope Creep ultimately depend, beyond the listed reasons?
options: The size of the data warehouse
The project management practices in place and the experience of the Project Manager and business stakeholders
questions.explanation: Many other causes exist; it all depends on the project management practices in place and the experience of the Project Manager and business stakeholders.
